_README: The MPC SOS Fade bot on the MT5_FFT terminal (PU Prime demo). This file is the ONLY thing that decides which terminal, account, symbol and strategy VERSION this bot trades — nothing is read from strategies/python/mpc_sos_fade/config.py, so lab experiments cannot reach it. No secrets live here: the MT5 password is in algos/credentials.json under mt5_accounts, and Telegram routing falls back to the shared group. Every broker fact below was MEASURED off the running terminal on 2026-07-31, not typed from memory — see _measured.
_measured: Probed against the live MT5_FFT terminal on 2026-07-31 (it was running, authorized, trading enabled). Account 700107749 / PUPrime-Demo / USD / balance 2000.00 / DEMO / hedging / leverage 500. XAUUSD.s: visible, digits 2, point 0.01, contract 100 oz, tick value $1.00, volume 0.01-100.00 step 0.01, spread 33 points ($0.33), trade_mode FULL, filling IOC (NOT FOK — market orders send IOC, pendings send RETURN, both fine). SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL = 20 points = $0.20: the broker itself refuses a stop closer than that to the entry.
_broker_tz_offsets: MEASURED, not assumed: the terminal's tick clock read +3.00h vs UTC on 2026-07-31, which is the DST half of '2,3'. The WINTER half (+2) is inferred from the standard PU Prime schedule and is NOT yet verified — re-measure with backtest/tools/compare_feeds.py after the November changeover, because a wrong offset shifts every session boundary the strategy trades off and nothing downstream can detect it.
_exec_risk_pct: SETTLED at 10% - Aaron's explicit call, 2026-08-05. This field previously read 'DECISION PENDING ... harmless while the bot is in dry run', and both halves went STALE the moment the bot was armed the same day: it is live, and 10% is now a deliberate acceptance rather than an unexamined default. A comment claiming a live bot is not trading is worse than no comment. The number it accepts: 10% measured a -54.9% max drawdown over 6.5 years, and Run 12 established that the drawdown is a losing STREAK at this risk rather than give-back, so risk % is the only lever that moves it. On this $2,000 demo account, 10% = $200 risked per trade. Re-open this only if the account purpose changes from demo.
_exec_min_stop_mode: ON at '% of price' 0.08 - Aaron's call 2026-08-05, after a 23-config sweep over 186,220 M15 bars (2018-09-13 -> 2026-08-04), ONE REAL REPLAY EACH (refusing a setup frees the single position slot, so the trade list reshuffles and no arithmetic over a finished list can stand in for a replay). Baseline 183 trades / +134.75R. 0.08 -> 181 / +136.75R (+2.00R). 0.10 -> 176 / +132.92R (-1.84R). 0.15 costs 25R, 0.30 costs 48R. It was briefly shipped at 0.10 earlier the same day; that was a measured mistake and this corrects it. WARNING - a small floor GAINS R for a mechanical reason, not a lucky one: the three tightest stops in 7.9 years ($1.03 / $1.06 / $1.18) were all full -1.00R losers, and Fixed $1.25 refuses exactly those three for exactly +3.00R. WARNING - do NOT read +2R as an edge. The jitter audit measured this strategy's run-to-run spread at sd 15.06R, so every value from 0.05 to 0.08 is statistically indistinguishable from zero and from each other. 0.08 is chosen as the HIGHEST value that does not start costing, i.e. the most protection for nothing. It is a SAFETY choice, not a profit one. WARNING - 'x ATR(14)' was measured and is the WRONG TOOL for this hazard: at 0.35 and 0.40 it never refuses the $1.03 stop at all, because that bar was quiet and $1.03 was not tight RELATIVE TO ATR. The hazard is qty = risk / stop_distance, which is pure price units - volatility does not enter it, so ATR blocks a different set of trades than the one at risk. WARNING - Pine parity is proven with this filter FIRING (block code 7 raised 213 times in a 21,899-bar export, compare_strategy.py exit 0 at warmups 100/500/1000/2000) but at 0.30, not at 0.08 - same code path, same px*val/100 floor, same refusal, same block code, only the constant differs. State it that way rather than claiming 0.08 was itself diffed. WARNING - it does not replace the two independent backstops: the broker's own 20-point SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL rejects a degenerate stop at the terminal, and place_pending_limit refuses one before it is sent. This guard is the one acting on OUR side of the wire, which is where the position is SIZED.
_account_profile: puprime_standard matches this broker (contract 100, mintick 0.01, no commission, swap modelled). It is INERT live — it only prices fills when fill_model is 'tick', which the bridge refuses. Set correctly anyway so the file never claims Vantage while trading PU Prime.
_strategy_source_hash: Content hash of strategies/python/mpc_sos_fade as promoted in commit 8fb2986. The bot re-hashes on startup and REFUSES to run if the code moved. Newlines are normalised before hashing — without that the Windows VPS (core.autocrlf=true rewrites every newline on checkout) computed a different number for identical code and the pin refused to start every time; verified matching on both machines 2026-07-31.
_magic: Unique to this bot. Every order it places carries it and every order it reads back is filtered by it — this is what stops two bots on one terminal cancelling each other's orders. MT5_FFT currently holds 0 positions and 0 orders.
_telegram: Both empty = the shared token and group from algos/credentials.json. Set telegram_chat_id to give this bot its own feed; set telegram_token_key (a KEY NAME in credentials.json, never a token) to give it its own Telegram identity.
